title: Species in News and the IUCN Red List

cards.h: Species in news is a Prelims staple
cards.b:
Almost every Prelims paper has a question on a species: its status, habitat or the park where it lives. UPSC picks animals that were in the news. The method is simple: learn the IUCN status, the Schedule and the place.

This lesson gives the system and the animals that recur most.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature was founded in 1948 and is based in Gland, Switzerland. It is a union of states and NGOs. Its Red List of Threatened Species is the main global record of extinction risk.

The Red List is a scientific assessment, not a law. It does not protect a species by itself. Indian protection comes from the Wildlife (Protection) Act and CITES.

From worst to best: Extinct (EX), Extinct in the Wild (EW), Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), Vulnerable (VU), Near Threatened (NT), Least Concern (LC). Two more: Data Deficient (DD) and Not Evaluated (NE).

Threatened means CR, EN and VU together. Criteria use population decline, range size, population size and extinction probability.

The Red List now covers well over 170,000 species, and roughly 28 percent of those assessed are threatened. The October 2025 update listed about 172,600 species assessed, of which about 48,600 (around 28%) are threatened.

Positive news exists. In October 2025 the green turtle was moved from Endangered to Least Concern globally after conservation gains.

• Tiger: Endangered.
  • Asiatic lion: Endangered.
  • Asian elephant: Endangered.
  • Indian rhino: Vulnerable.
  • Snow leopard: Vulnerable.
  • Cheetah: Vulnerable globally.
  • Ganges river dolphin: Endangered.

The IUCN Red List is revised through the year, so these statuses can change. The snow leopard was moved from Endangered to Vulnerable in 2017. The Asiatic lion lives only in Gir and its surroundings in Gujarat. The Ganges river dolphin is India's National Aquatic Animal, and the Indian rhino is found mainly in Assam.

• Great Indian Bustard: Critically Endangered, mainly Rajasthan.
  • Gharial: Critically Endangered, mainly in the Chambal.
  • Pygmy hog: Critically Endangered, Assam.
  • White-rumped, Indian and slender-billed vultures: Critically Endangered.
  • Hangul (Kashmir stag): Critically Endangered, Dachigam.
  • Sangai (brow-antlered deer) is Endangered.

A species' status changes with new assessments, so always check the latest IUCN list. Vultures collapsed in the 1990s after cattle were treated with the drug diclofenac, which poisoned birds that fed on carcasses; the veterinary use was banned in 2006. The Great Indian Bustard faces deaths from collisions with power lines. The pygmy hog is bred in captivity at Basistha near Guwahati and released in Assam grasslands.

CITES (1973, in force 1975) regulates trade. Appendix I bans commercial trade in species threatened with extinction. Appendix II allows controlled trade. Appendix III lists species a country asks others to help protect.

CMS (Bonn, 1979) protects migratory species. India hosted CMS COP13 at Gandhinagar in February 2020 (Great Indian Bustard was a theme). The Wildlife Act 2022 now has a schedule for CITES specimens.

CITES works through permits: exporting a listed specimen needs a permit from the exporting country's authority. India has been a party since 1976. Under CMS, Appendix I lists migratory species in danger, while Appendix II lists those that need international agreements. Regional agreements and MoUs, such as the Siberian Crane MoU, follow from it. India has been a CMS party since 1983.

Charismatic animals attract funds: tigers, lions, elephants. Plants, insects and amphibians are far more threatened but get little attention.

Critics also say the Red List status is global. A species may be Least Concern globally yet be rare in India. Local lists and the national Schedules therefore matter.

When a species is in the news, ask five things: Red List status, Wildlife Act Schedule, habitat state, threat, and any project (Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, Project Dolphin, Great Indian Bustard recovery).

India’s Wildlife Act Schedule I gives the highest protection; the 2022 amendment kept it for the most endangered. The Great Indian Bustard also gained attention in a 2021 Supreme Court case on power lines in its habitat.

Mains-style: “What is the role of the IUCN Red List in conservation planning? Mention its limits.” Structure: purpose; categories; how India uses it; limits (global scale, data gaps, not legally binding); conclusion.

Mains-style: “Why do species like the Great Indian Bustard survive in the face of development pressure?”

Prelims tip: Learn the “CR list”: GIB, gharial, pygmy hog, hangul, three vultures. Remember threatened = CR + EN + VU.

quiz.q: Which category is the highest threat level before extinction in the wild?
quiz.w: CR is above EN and VU on the ladder.
